q: The Dow rose 3.01% while the Nasdaq rose 6.51%. What best explains the gap?
options: The Dow was dragged down by a jump in the 10-year yield
The Nasdaq holds more consumer stocks that investors rushed into
The Nasdaq holds more AI-linked giants that Huang's return lifted most
The Dow holds more energy producers that fell with crude prices
explain: Nvidia and the companies that depend on its spending carry heavy weight in the Nasdaq, so the AI relief rally showed up there most. The 10-year yield rose only 1 basis point, so it wasn't a drag.

q: Kroger and Tyson Foods were among the S&P 500's biggest losers while Nvidia soared. What best explains that?
options: A jump in bond yields made grocery stocks less appealing
Investors sold steady defensive names to buy growth as fear faded
Higher oil prices raised their costs and hurt their profit outlook
Lawmakers started targeting food companies after Huang's return
explain: Investors had been hiding in safe stocks during the AI scare, so when fear faded they sold those shelters to buy tech. Oil actually fell 4.23% and the 10-year yield barely moved.

q: The BOJ chief has signaled a near-term hike. If the BOJ raises rates and narrows its gap with the Fed's 3.875%, what would USD/JPY, now 158.93, probably do?
options: Up
Down
explain: A higher Japanese rate makes holding yen more rewarding, so fewer traders sell yen for dollars and the yen strengthens. That pushes USD/JPY down.

q: Fed officials sound more hawkish about oil-driven inflation than traders expected. What would the 2-year yield, now 4.63%, probably do?
options: Up
Down
explain: The 2-year yield tracks expected Fed rates over the next two years, so tougher talk pushes it up. The San Francisco Fed research says the 10-year would react less because the inflation is supply-driven.

q: Reports of a formal SEC action against Nvidia hit while the VIX sits at 26.62. What would the VIX probably do?
options: Up
Down
explain: The rebound rests on the AI trade feeling safe again, so legal trouble at Nvidia would bring nerves back. Traders then pay more for protection and the VIX rises.

q: Put today's AI stock chain in the right cause-and-effect order.
items: Nvidia's board approves Huang's return
Nvidia, Oracle and CoreWeave jump
S&P 500 posts its best day in over a year
VIX falls 25.83%
explain: The personnel news came first, the AI-linked stocks reacted, their weight lifted the index, and the calmer market drained fear from the VIX.

q: Put today's oil chain in the right cause-and-effect order.
items: Gulf crude keeps flowing despite tanker attacks
WTI closes at its lowest since August
Gas prices and inflation pressure ease
Fed has less reason to hike
explain: Steady supply came first, so crude got cheaper, which eases inflation worries and gives the Fed a bit more room to wait.

q: The dollar index rose 0.49% to 104.32 mainly because investors reacted to the Democratic midterm rout.
options: True
False
explain: The midterms started the dollar conversation, but headlines credit hawkish Fed bets for today's gain.

q: The 2-year yield at 4.63% sitting well above the Fed's 3.875% rate suggests traders expect the Fed's next move to be a hike.
options: True
False
explain: Short-term yields follow expected policy rates, so a 2-year yield about 75 basis points above the Fed's rate means traders are betting on higher rates.

q: The St. Louis Fed found that the big AI spenders' debt compared with assets rose from about 25% in 2023 to nearly 30% in early 2026.
options: True
False
explain: The direction is backwards. Their ratio fell from nearly 30% to roughly 25%, so the spending has been funded mostly from profits.

q: Fed officials talked about higher rates over time, yet the 10-year yield rose only 1 basis point to 4.92%. Which explanation fits best?
options: Bond traders ignored the Fed because the stock rally absorbed all the buying
Williams said inflation will near 2% in 2027, which erased every hike bet
The 2-year yield fell enough to cancel out the rise in long-term yields
Oil-driven inflation is a supply problem, so Fed surprises reach long-term yields less
explain: The San Francisco Fed letter found Fed surprises pass through to longer yields mainly when inflation is demand-driven. Hike bets haven't disappeared, since the 2-year still sits well above the Fed's rate.

q: Cook warned that damaged infrastructure and low inventories could keep oil prices high for a long time. Why does that matter after WTI's 4.23% drop?
options: It means oil company stocks should fall more than crude itself
It suggests the relief could fade, so inflation worries might return
It shows Gulf tankers have stopped moving, which explains the drop
It means the Fed will cut rates now that oil is cheaper
explain: Today's drop came from steady flows, but Cook's point is that the underlying supply is still fragile. That means cheaper oil may not last, and neither would the relief for inflation.

q: The VIX fell 25.83% to 26.62. What does that say about the mood in the market?
options: Traders are buying more protection because the index rose so far
Traders expect smaller swings than before, but nerves are still high
Traders expect the S&P 500 to keep rising after such a big jump
Traders see volatility as gone now that the index has bounced back
explain: A falling VIX means traders expect calmer markets, so fear drained out. The level is still elevated, so the market hasn't fully relaxed.

q: Why does the gap between the Fed's 3.875% and the BOJ's 1.25% keep pressure on the yen?
options: Low Japanese rates push foreign investors to buy yen as a haven
Japan prints extra yen to buy dollars whenever rates diverge
Japan sells dollars each day until the rate gap closes by itself
Holding dollars pays more than holding yen, so traders sell yen
explain: A 2.625 percentage point gap rewards traders for holding dollars instead of yen, so they sell yen. Japan's intervention goes the other way, since it sells dollars to buy yen.

q: A New York Fed note says U.S. labor supply may soon shrink. Why does that matter for the Fed's energy inflation worry?
options: Fewer workers lets wages rise, so energy inflation could spread to services
Fewer workers means higher company profits, so stocks would rise
Fewer workers lowers growth, so the Fed would cut rates sooner
Fewer workers means less oil demand, so inflation would cool faster
explain: When employers compete for fewer workers, wages can rise, which can keep service prices climbing. That's exactly the leak into wages and services that central banks fear from the oil shock.

q: The ECB said it expects to publish the details of its new collateral requirements for tokenised assets in spring 2027, with implementation planned for June 2027.
options: True
False
explain: That's right, which is why the decision is slow plumbing news rather than something that moves rates or the euro today.

q: The Dow rose 0.85% while the Nasdaq fell 1.48%. Which explanation fits best?
options: Investors left stocks and moved the cash into Treasuries
Dell's strong report lifted every stock except Nvidia's
Investors sold expensive AI names and bought other sectors
Higher oil prices hurt tech companies more than industrials
explain: Money rotated away from AI-linked names into other parts of the market, so the Dow rose. Treasuries barely moved, since the 10-year yield changed only 1 basis point.

q: The 10-year yield barely moved even though the Nasdaq fell 1.48%. What best explains the lack of a bond rally?
options: Traders still expect Fed hikes, so inflation worries offset safety buying
Foreign governments sold Treasuries to support the weak yen
Gold's drop pulled money out of bonds at the same time
The Fed's discount rate minutes showed a surprise policy change
explain: The 2-year yield at 4.63% sits well above the Fed's 3.875%, which means hikes are expected. That inflation worry cancels the usual rush into bonds when stocks fall.

q: Anthropic closed Tuesday above its $83 IPO price after sliding from its $111.50 open on Nov 19.
options: True
False
explain: Anthropic fell 6.5% to $81.91, which is below the $83 IPO price.

q: Suppose traders become more sure that the Fed will raise rates in December. What would gold probably do?
options: Up
Down
explain: Many beginners expect gold to rise as a safe haven, but gold pays no interest. Higher expected rates make it less attractive, which is why it fell 2.72% today.

q: Put the AI trade story from Monday to Tuesday in the right order.
items: Huang's return as Nvidia CEO is approved
The Nasdaq jumps 6.51% on Monday
Regulatory questions and the investigation stay unresolved
Nvidia and Anthropic fall sharply on Tuesday
explain: The comeback sparked a big rally, but the unresolved questions and high prices let buyers sell the bounce quickly.

q: Dell's sales more than doubled and it announced a $25 billion buyback, yet AI stocks still fell. What does that suggest?
options: Good news was already priced in, so it could not lift the group
Dell's results were weaker than analysts had feared
Dell is too small to matter to the broader AI group
Buybacks tell investors that a company's stock will fall
explain: When expectations are already high, even strong results may not push prices higher. That fits the worry that AI valuations are stretched.

q: The Bank of Japan's chief has signaled a near-term rate hike. If Japan raises rates toward the Fed's level, what would USD/JPY probably do?
options: Up
Down
explain: With USD/JPY at 159.23, it might seem due to keep rising. A smaller gap between the BOJ's 1.25% and the Fed's 3.875% gives people less reason to sell yen, so USD/JPY would likely fall.

q: The Fed will discuss the economic outlook on Dec 9 and make its policy decision on Dec 8.
options: True
False
explain: It is the other way around: the outlook is discussed on Dec 8 and the policy decision comes on Dec 9.

q: The San Francisco Fed says oil-driven inflation is mostly supply-driven. What does that imply for Fed surprises?
options: They make short-term and long-term yields move exactly together
They move long-term yields more than in demand-driven episodes
They make the Fed act faster than it would on demand inflation
They move long-term yields less than in demand-driven episodes
explain: Policy surprises mostly pass through to longer-term rates when inflation is demand-driven. With supply-driven inflation, the long end should react less, so the 2-year may move more than the 10-year.

q: Why did CIBC say the Bank of Canada could hike again in December?
options: Canada's growth is booming after the US midterm result
Macklem keeps stressing persistent inflation despite signs of easing
The Fed asked other central banks to hike alongside it
The Canadian dollar hit a 19-month low and needs support
explain: CIBC pointed to Governor Macklem's continued concern about persistent inflation. The Canadian dollar's weakness was a market move, not the stated reason.

q: The dollar index fell 0.47%, yet USD/JPY rose 0.19% to 159.23. What best explains the yen's weakness?
options: Japan's 1.25% rate is far below the Fed's 3.875%
Japan resumed record intervention, which pushes the yen lower
The Bank of Japan cut rates at its latest meeting
Japan's trade surplus grew, so exporters sold yen
explain: The big rate gap encourages selling yen to hold higher-paying dollars. Intervention means buying yen, and Japan actually posted a sixth straight trade deficit.

q: Put this oil to Fed chain in the right order.
items: Oil prices fall from their highs
Pump prices drop to the lowest since March
Headline inflation cools
The Fed has more room to wait on hikes
explain: Cheaper oil lowers gasoline prices, which cools headline inflation and gives the Fed more patience. Cook's warning about low inventories means the relief might not last.

q: If AI sentiment keeps falling, what would credit spreads on heavily indebted data center builders probably do?
options: Up
Down
explain: Spreads widen when lenders want more extra interest for risk. The St. Louis Fed found that data center builders lean more on debt than the giants do, so they would feel the strain first.

q: The St. Louis Fed found that big tech firms' debt compared with assets rose above the 34% level of other firms as they funded AI.
options: True
False
explain: Hyperscalers' ratio fell from nearly 30% in 2023 to roughly 25% in early 2026, below the other firms' 34%. They are funding the boom mostly with their own profits.

q: Why does the BNP Paribas memory chip warning feed the wider AI worry?
options: Chipmakers would have to raise prices to cover higher borrowing
Weak memory demand shows consumers cutting spending on phones
Falling chip prices would cut profits at a core AI group
Micron's drop raised the 10-year yield and hit tech valuations
explain: If too many chips are built, prices fall and chipmakers earn less. Chip stocks are a core part of the AI trade, and the semiconductor index had already fallen about 36%.

q: Goldman expects the dollar rally to continue in coming months but calls the dollar overbought. How does that fit today's move?
options: Fed hike bets have vanished, so the dollar has lost its support
The dollar must rise every day until it reaches the next big level
The rally is over and the dollar will fall all through 2027
A short pause like the 0.47% dip is normal while the trend stays up
explain: Overbought means a rally has run fast and may pause, not that it is finished. J.P. Morgan and Goldman both still see dollar strength if the Fed keeps leaning toward hikes.

q: The Dow rose 0.33% while the Nasdaq fell 0.62%. What best explains the gap between them?
options: Oil's 2.21% jump hurt tech profits more than it hurt industrial companies
AI-linked tech stocks sold off hard while the rest of the market held up
Falling yields cut the value of every tech stock but left others alone
The tariff plan applied only to Nasdaq-listed firms and spared the Dow
explain: The AI giants carry so much weight in the Nasdaq that their selloff dragged it down, while the Dow holds fewer of them. Falling yields would normally help tech, not hurt it.

q: The 10-year yield fell 6 bp to 4.85% on the day PCE inflation matched a hot 3.8%. What best explains the drop?
options: Investors expected the Fed to cut rates in December after seeing the data
Third quarter growth was revised lower, which cooled the economic outlook
Heavy selling in bonds pushed their prices up, which pulled yields lower
Nervous stock investors and tariff worries sent money into Treasuries
explain: The AI selloff and the tariff plan pushed investors toward safety, and buying Treasuries lifts their price and lowers the yield. Growth was actually revised up to 4.3%, and a December cut looks like a long shot.

q: PCE inflation matched forecasts at 3.8% and yields still fell, which suggests the inflation data was not the main driver of bonds today.
options: True
False
explain: A number that matches forecasts holds no surprise, so it can't explain a 6 bp move. Fear in stocks and tariff worries fit the move better.

q: The Fed's 3.875% rate sits far above 3.8% inflation, so policy is clearly holding prices back.
options: True
False
explain: The rate is only about a tenth of a point above inflation, so policy is barely restrictive in real terms. That is why the Fed has little room to cut.

q: The dollar index rose to a fresh 20-month high after the US announced its new tariff plan.
options: True
False
explain: The dollar index slipped 0.07% to 103.74 after giving up early gains, and the 20-month high came earlier in the week. Tariffs and falling yields pulled it back.

q: The VIX climbed 7.32% to 28.29 even though the S&P 500 fell only 0.25%, so investors were still paying up for protection.
options: True
False
explain: A VIX near 28 on a quiet-looking index day shows nervousness stayed high after the early tech selloff. The index recovering did not make people relax.

q: Nvidia drops sharply again and the VIX jumps. If the pattern of today repeats, what would the 10-year yield probably do?
options: Up
Down
explain: Many beginners expect yields to follow stocks, but fear sends money into Treasuries instead. More buying lifts bond prices and pushes yields lower, as the 6 bp drop showed today.

q: The Bank of Japan hikes its 1.25% rate while the Fed stays at 3.875%. What would USD/JPY probably do from 159.26?
options: Up
Down
explain: A hike narrows the 2.625 point gap, so holding yen becomes more rewarding and the dollar buys fewer yen. USD/JPY down means a stronger yen.

q: Middle East tension pushes WTI well above 83.86 while inflation stays near 3.8%. What would happen to market bets on a Fed hike?
options: Up
Down
explain: Pricier oil feeds headline inflation, and the Fed is already boxed in with its rate barely above inflation. That makes hike bets stronger and cut hopes weaker.

q: Put today's fear chain in cause-to-effect order.
items: Nvidia gives back much of Monday's rally
The VIX rises 7.32% to 28.29
Investors buy Treasuries for safety
The 10-year yield falls 6 bp to 4.85%
explain: The AI selloff creates the fear, the VIX measures it, and the move into Treasuries pushes bond prices up and yields down.

q: Put the energy inflation chain in cause-to-effect order.
items: Middle East tension lifts WTI 2.21% to 83.86
Energy costs feed into headline inflation
The Fed has little room to cut in December
Stocks priced for easier 2027 money get exposed
explain: Oil is the starting link, inflation is the middle, and the Fed's lack of room to cut is what puts stocks at risk.

q: The SF Fed paper says supply-driven inflation like energy has grown since the pandemic. What does that imply about Fed surprises?
options: They will move long-term yields less than they used to in the past
They will matter only for the dollar and not for Treasury markets
They will move long-term yields more because energy costs hit everyone
They will stop moving short-term interest rates altogether from now on
explain: The paper finds surprises pass through to longer-term forward rates mainly when inflation is demand-driven. With more supply pressure, long-term yields should react less, so the front end does more of the work.

q: Vanda Research says retail investors who bought Nvidia on the dip last week have nearly lost their gains. What does that mean for the AI trade?
options: Retail buyers sold early, so the AI rally has more room to run
The cushion under AI stocks is thin, so another drop could trigger selling
Huang's return was reversed, which undid the bounce all by itself
Nvidia's earnings fell short, which wiped out last week's gains
explain: When recent buyers are back near breakeven, a further drop puts them at a loss, and some may sell. That makes the market more fragile.

q: The BOJ's rate is 2.625 points below the Fed's, and USD/JPY ended at 159.26. Why does that gap keep pressure on the yen?
options: The gap forces Japan to intervene in the market every single day
A higher Fed rate makes Japanese bonds riskier than US Treasuries
Holding dollars pays far more than holding yen, so investors sell yen
Japan's trade surplus is growing, so there are too many yen around
explain: Higher US rates reward people for holding dollars, which encourages selling yen, and the same logic makes yen borrowing like Berkshire's attractive. Japan actually posted a sixth straight trade deficit, not a surplus.

q: Gold rose 1.85% to 3,627.8 while yields and the dollar slipped. Which link fits today best?
options: Hot PCE data raised hike bets, which usually helps gold the most
Money left stocks after Nvidia recovered, so gold became the new trade
Gold pays no interest, so lower yields make it cheaper to hold
A stronger dollar made gold cheaper for buyers using other currencies
explain: With yields falling, the income given up by owning gold shrinks, and a softer dollar plus a nervous mood added support. Higher hike bets would normally weigh on gold, and the dollar was slightly lower.

q: The US proposed tariffs on 14 partners, and the dollar gave up early gains while yields fell. Which reading fits best?
options: The proposal was ignored, and the dollar's slide came from the PCE data
Investors expected tariffs to lift prices, so they priced in more Fed hikes
China and the EU cut their rates, which weakened the dollar's appeal
Worries about growth and trade outweighed worries about higher prices
explain: Tariffs can push inflation up or growth down, and today the market leaned toward the growth worry. That shows in falling yields and a softer dollar, while the PCE number simply matched forecasts.
